verses.1: For the music director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David.
verses.2: The wicked declare: "Sin is in my heart. There is no fear of God before my eyes."
verses.3: For he has plotted deceit in his sight to find his guilt to hate.
verses.4: The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit; he has not learned to do good.
verses.5: He plans evil on his bed, stands ready on every evil path, and does not despise wickedness.
verses.6: The LORD, your steadfast love is in the heavens; your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
verses.7: Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; your judgments are like the deep, vast. The LORD will save both man and beast.
verses.8: How precious is your steadfast love, O God! All people take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
verses.9: They are satisfied with the abundance of your house, and you water them with the stream of your delights.
verses.10: For with you is the source of life; in your light, we see light.
verses.11: Extend your steadfast love to those who know you, and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
verses.12: Let not the foot of the arrogant come near to me, and let not the hand of the wicked move me.
verses.13: There have fallen all the workers of iniquity, driven out and unable to rise.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "The wicked declare" — the Hebrew construction פֹּהֵ֥שׁ is used in a direct quotation, hence the shift to quotation marks.
- v. 3: "to find his guilt to hate" — the phrase לִמְצֹֽא עֲוֺנוֹ לִשְׂנֹֽא is rendered to reflect the sequence of finding and then hating.
- v. 13: "driven out and unable to rise" — the Hebrew uses a poetic parallelism with "fell" and "driven out" to reinforce the idea of complete downfall.
